Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
The property <MATH_0002>``<MATH_0003> is quasi-separated''
is fpqc local on the base on algebraic spaces over <MATH_0004>.

A base change of a quasi-separated morphism is quasi-separated, see
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0001>.
Hence the direct implication in
Definition <REF_0002>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Let <MATH_0001> be an fpqc covering of algebraic spaces over <MATH_0002>.
Let <MATH_0003> be a morphism of algebraic spaces over <MATH_0004>.
Assume each base change <MATH_0005> is quasi-separated.
This means that each of the morphisms
<MATH_0006>
is quasi-compact. The base change of a fpqc covering is an fpqc covering, see
Topologies on Spaces, Lemma <REF_0003>
hence <MATH_0007>
is an fpqc covering of algebraic spaces. Moreover, each
<MATH_0008> is the base change of the morphism
<MATH_0009>. Hence it follows from
Lemma <REF_0004>
that <MATH_0010> is quasi-compact, i.e., <MATH_0011> is quasi-separated.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
The property <MATH_0002>``<MATH_0003> is universally closed''
is fpqc local on the base on algebraic spaces over <MATH_0004>.

We will use
Lemma <REF_0001>
to prove this. Assumptions (1) and (2) of that lemma follow from
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0002>.
Let <MATH_0001> be a surjective flat morphism of affine schemes over <MATH_0002>.
Let <MATH_0003> be a morphism of algebraic spaces, and assume
that the base change <MATH_0004> is universally closed.
We have to show that <MATH_0005> is universally closed. To see this, using
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0003>
again, it is enough to show that for every affine scheme <MATH_0006> and
morphism <MATH_0007> the map <MATH_0008> is closed.
Consider the cube (<REF_0004>).
The assumption that <MATH_0009> is universally closed implies that
<MATH_0010> is closed.
As <MATH_0011> is quasi-compact, surjective, and flat
as a base change of <MATH_0012>
we see the map <MATH_0013> is submersive, see
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0005>.
Moreover the map
<MATH_0014>
is surjective, see
Properties of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0006>.
It follows by elementary topology that <MATH_0015> is closed.
